title: Trace
description: The append-only record of one agent cycle run under one Grant. One JSON object per line in .hexagen/evidence/trace.jsonl. See docs/kernel/TRACE.md. Never redefines Grant — grant_id must equal some Grant.id (docs/kernel/grant.schema.json). Three record kinds: the greenfield line (unchanged), the brownfield line (adds seq and prev_hash), and grant_missing (a denial with no grant_id). In the brownfield kinds, seq and prev_hash are both present or both absent.

grant_id.description: Must equal some Grant's `id`. A Trace whose grant_id matches nothing is invalid evidence, not a trace with an unknown grant to be tolerated. Never a second identity independent of the Grant that authorized this cycle.

goal_id.description: Opaque identifier for whatever prompted this cycle (a work-plan row, a ticket, a project thread id). Not defined further by this schema.

tool_calls.description: Every tool call the cycle made, in the order it made them.

name.description: Tool name, as it appears in the owning Grant's `tools`.

args_digest.description: Digest of the call's arguments (e.g. "sha256:<hex>"), not the arguments themselves. Trace is evidence of what ran, not a payload store.

result_digest.description: Digest of the call's result, same reasoning as args_digest.

time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of this specific call. Checked against the owning Grant's expires_at/revoked_at under the fail-closed rules in TRACE.md: a call at or after revoked_at is invalid (revocation is immediate); a call strictly after expires_at is invalid (a call exactly at expires_at is still in-window and valid).

halt_reason.description: Why the cycle stopped. Not a closed enum (a kit adapter may need its own reasons), but TRACE.md names a shared vocabulary to reuse: completed, grant_denied, grant_expired, grant_revoked, budget_exceeded, error.

transaction_ids.description: Transaction ids (from @hexagen/transaction-system) this cycle created or touched, in the order they were touched. Ties this Trace to the transaction manager's own record of what those transactions did, without duplicating their contents.

started_at.description: ISO 8601. Should be at or before every tool_calls[].time and at or before ended_at.

ended_at.description: ISO 8601. Should be at or after every tool_calls[].time and at or after started_at.

greenfield_line.description: Greenfield line: unchanged from before the brownfield bump. No seq, no prev_hash.

ended_at.description: ISO 8601. Should be at or after every tool_calls[].time and at or after started_at.

seq.description: Position of this line in the brownfield trace chain, starting at 0 for genesis.

prev_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous line's canonical bytes (sorted-key JSON, including that line's prev_hash), as 64 lowercase hex characters. The genesis line uses 64 zeros.

brownfield_line.description: Brownfield line: today's line plus seq and prev_hash, which chain it to the line before it.

grant_missing.description: A call that carried no grant, or a grant with no id, was denied. It has no grant_id to cite, so it is its own record kind rather than a line with an empty grant_id. Never evidence of a write.

seq.description: Position of this line in the brownfield trace chain, starting at 0 for genesis.

prev_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous line's canonical bytes (sorted-key JSON, including that line's prev_hash), as 64 lowercase hex characters. The genesis line uses 64 zeros.

goal_id.description: Opaque identifier for whatever prompted this cycle (a work-plan row, a ticket, a project thread id). Not defined further by this schema.

tool.description: The tool the denied call tried to use.

args_digest.description: Digest of the call's arguments (e.g. "sha256:<hex>"), not the arguments themselves. Trace is evidence of what ran, not a payload store.

reason.description: Why the call was denied (e.g. no grant supplied, grant without an id).

time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the denied call.
